speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are suffering from sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg. To help me understand your condition, have you been experiencing numbness, tingling, or any weakness in the affected leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic "slipped disc" or herniated nucleus pulposus, especially given the sudden onset during exercise and radiation to the foot. Did the pain occur immediately after a specific movement, like lifting a weight or bending over?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lumbar Herniated Disc (Sciatica). The sudden onset during exercise with sharp pain radiating to the foot is highly characteristic of a disc herniation compressing the nerve root. I recommend an MRI of the lumbar spine to confirm the location and severity of the herniation.
